title: Is Testosterone a Steroid? | Phoenix
summary: Testosterone is a steroid hormone. Learn how prescribed treatment differs from steroid misuse and how testing works for Canadian men. - Nov 24, 2026
body_markdown:
Men searching for answers on low testosterone often hit the same wall: is this a hormone the body needs, or a steroid to be wary of? The testes produce testosterone naturally every day, and a prescription managed by a licensed provider involves that same hormone, with dosing set by the provider based on bloodwork. The confusion usually comes from lumping that process in with anabolic steroid misuse, which is a very different scale and story. We'll sort out the chemistry, the risks, and how testing and treatment work in Canada.


**TLDR:**


- Testosterone is chemically a steroid hormone, but TRT and anabolic steroid misuse differ in dose and oversight.
- Anabolic steroid misuse often involves doses 10 to 100 times higher than therapeutic amounts, per the DEA.
- Peptides are amino acid chains, a different molecule family from steroid hormones, and products sold online raise their own quality concerns.
- Testing comes first: a blood test and a licensed provider's review guide whether treatment fits.
- Phoenix connects Canadian men with licensed healthcare providers for testosterone-related blood testing and consultation.


## Is Testosterone a Steroid or a Hormone?


Testosterone is both. That is the short answer, and it is the part most searches skip over.


Chemically, testosterone belongs to the steroid hormone family. Steroid, in biology, means a molecule built from a cholesterol backbone, and testosterone fits that definition the same way estrogen and cortisol do.


The confusion starts with the slang version of "steroid," tied to anabolic steroid abuse. The DEA notes that anabolic steroids are synthetic variants of the naturally occurring male hormone testosterone, made and used at doses far beyond what the body produces on its own, often for non-medical reasons such as athletic or appearance goals ([DEA Drug Fact Sheet](https://www.dea.gov/sites/default/files/2020-06/Steroids-2020_0.pdf) ).


The structure is shared, but dose and oversight are not. Testosterone the body makes naturally, or a prescription a licensed healthcare provider manages, is a medically supervised hormone treatment. Using a black market vial at multiples of a therapeutic dose is anabolic steroid abuse. Same molecule family, very different story.


## What Testosterone Does In The Male Body


Testosterone is the main sex hormone in men. The testes produce most of it, with a smaller amount coming from the adrenal glands, two organs sitting above the kidneys.


Once in the bloodstream, testosterone acts on tissue throughout the body. It plays a role in:


- Building and maintaining muscle mass
- Supporting bone density
- Supporting libido and sexual function
- Influencing mood and energy
- Supporting red blood cell production


Levels typically peak in early adulthood and[decline gradually with age](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/testosterone-levels-men-after-40) , a normal pattern, not a sign something has gone wrong.


When levels sit in a healthy range, men often notice steadier energy, a more consistent sex drive, and an easier time maintaining muscle through regular training. Individual experience varies based on genetics, lifestyle, and overall health.


## Testosterone Vs. Anabolic Steroids: What Sets Them Apart


The split between testosterone therapy and anabolic steroid misuse comes down to three things: how much you take, who is supervising it, and why.


Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is a prescription treatment. A licensed healthcare provider orders bloodwork, reviews symptoms, and decides whether treatment fits, then adjusts the plan based on follow-up results.


Anabolic steroid misuse looks different. The DEA notes that doses abused for muscle building or performance are often[far higher](https://www.dea.gov/factsheets/steroids) than approved therapeutic amounts. There is no diagnosis behind it and no provider adjusting the plan.


TRT Anabolic Steroid Misuse


Dose Set by a licensed provider based on bloodwork Far above therapeutic range


Oversight Licensed provider, bloodwork None


Purpose Prescribed only after a provider assessment and bloodwork Non-medical use without a diagnosis


Legal status Prescription required Often unregulated or illicit


Dose and supervision change the entire risk picture, even when the starting molecule is the same.


## Is Testosterone Cypionate A Steroid?


Testosterone cypionate is one of the most common injectable forms of testosterone, made by attaching a cypionate ester to the testosterone molecule. Which form suits an individual, if any, is a decision for a licensed healthcare provider.


Yes, it is a steroid in the chemical sense, the same cholesterol-based structure as any other form of testosterone. It is also a controlled substance in Canada, governed under the federal framework that oversees controlled substances nationwide ([Controlled Drugs and Substances Act](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/c-38.8/page-12.html) ), meaning a prescription from a licensed provider is required.


Outside medical care, testosterone products are sometimes used without a prescription at doses far beyond what a provider would prescribe. A high dose carries different risk depending on context: a provider-managed plan for one person, or an unsupervised dose for another. Dosing and injection frequency should be set by a licensed provider based on bloodwork and symptoms, not a forum thread.


## Peptides Vs. Steroids For Muscle Growth


Peptides are short chains of amino acids, the building blocks of protein. That structure sets them apart from steroid hormones like testosterone, which are built on a cholesterol backbone. Different molecule family, different mechanism, and peptides are not classified as steroids in bodybuilding or chemistry.


Sermorelin, CJC-1295, and ipamorelin are peptides often sold online with fitness claims. According to[Drugs.com](https://www.drugs.com/medical-answers/peptides-muscle-growth-what-evidence-show-safe-3583330/) , none are approved by the FDA for building muscle or athletic performance, and no human study has shown that any of these peptides builds muscle in healthy adults.


Legal status adds another layer of risk. Most products sold online as research peptides are not tested for purity, dose, or sterility, and in one analysis cited by Drugs.com, 42% to 71% of samples failed basic quality checks.


Combining peptides and steroids does not improve on that picture. There is no solid safety or efficacy data supporting the practice, just two categories of unsupervised dosing stacked on top of each other. Neither comes close to the oversight built into testosterone therapy managed by a licensed healthcare provider.


## Side Effects And Risks Of Testosterone Therapy


Testosterone therapy carries a real risk profile, separate from the risks tied to anabolic steroid misuse. Working with a licensed healthcare provider means those risks get monitored, not ignored.


Side effects reported with testosterone treatment can include acne, fluid retention, and changes in red blood cell count, which is why providers may order follow-up bloodwork. Mood changes, including irritability or anxiety, have also been reported.


A frequent question is whether a man can stop once he starts. Natural production can slow or stop during therapy, since the body senses enough hormone circulating and scales back its own output. Stopping is possible, but it should happen under medical guidance so a provider can manage symptoms as natural production recovers.


Anabolic steroid misuse carries a different scale of risk, tied to doses far beyond therapeutic range and no provider oversight to catch problems early.


## How Much Does Testosterone Treatment Cost


How much testosterone treatment costs depends on format, province, and whether lab work or consultations get bundled into the price. There is no single number that applies to everyone.


Injections, gels, and creams can carry different cost structures, and pricing varies by clinic, pharmacy, and dosing schedule. Some formats are billed monthly, while others need a larger ongoing supply, which may change what you pay over time.


Insurance can change the math, depending on your plan. With private coverage or a Health Spending Account, your out-of-pocket costs may be lower than the full price. Without coverage, you pay the full cost of the prescription plus any separate consultation or lab fees. Coverage rules can change, so confirm details with your plan as of late 2026.


A few factors shift the final price more than people expect:


- Province, since drug pricing and coverage rules are not uniform across Canada
- Whether bloodwork is bundled into a treatment package or billed on its own
- Whether consultations are one time or recurring
- Pharmacy markup, which varies by location


Prices change over time, so check Phoenix's[current testosterone treatment pricing](https://www.phoenix.ca/pricing) page, or confirm with your own provider or pharmacy, before budgeting around a specific figure.


## Natural Ways And Supplements To Increase Testosterone


Lifestyle habits tend to have better evidence than supplements for supporting healthy testosterone levels. Sleep ranks near the top, since much of the body's hormone activity follows a sleep cycle, and consistently short sleep may pull levels down, while[working out may help support testosterone](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/testosterone-and-exercise-research) alongside these habits. Resistance training,[keeping body weight in a healthy range](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/overweight-low-testosterone-men) , and managing chronic stress may also support balance, since excess fat tissue and high cortisol levels may work against testosterone production over time. Diet matters too: enough protein, healthy fats, zinc, and vitamin D supply raw material the body uses. These habits shift the odds over weeks and months, not overnight, and results vary from person to person.


Over the counter testosterone boosters are where the evidence gets thinner. Most combine herbal extracts, vitamins, and minerals. Published reviews suggest the evidence that these products raise testosterone in men with already normal levels is limited and inconsistent.


A few points worth keeping in mind:


- Supplements are not held to the same regulatory standard as prescription treatment, so dose and purity can vary between brands.
- Some ingredients carry their own side effects, including stomach upset, headaches, or interactions with other medications.
- Marketing claims on a label do not equal clinical proof.
- If fatigue, low libido, or other symptoms persist, a lab test provides more information than any supplement bottle will.


No over the counter product reliably replaces a diagnosed low testosterone treatment plan guided by a licensed healthcare provider.


## Getting Tested And Treated For Low Testosterone In Canada


Testing for low testosterone starts with a blood test, usually drawn in the morning when levels run highest. The test measures[total and free testosterone](https://www.phoenix.ca/labs/biomarkers) , the portion not bound to proteins and available for tissues to use. A single low reading is not automatically a diagnosis. Providers typically want a pattern from a[testosterone blood test](https://www.phoenix.ca/labs) , often paired with symptoms like fatigue, low libido, or trouble building muscle, before confirming low testosterone.


From there, the path to treatment depends on which route you take.


**Traditional, in-person route**


- Appointment with a family doctor, sometimes requiring a referral to an endocrinologist
- Blood draw at a separate lab visit
- Follow-up appointment to review results and discuss treatment


**Telehealth-based route**


- Online health questionnaire covering symptoms and medical history
- Lab requisition for blood work, often completed at a participating lab near you
- Licensed healthcare provider reviews results and determines next steps, usually through secure messaging instead of an in-person visit


Both paths rely on the same bloodwork and the same clinical judgment from a licensed provider. A traditional appointment means scheduling around clinic hours and sitting in a waiting room, which can be a barrier for men who would rather avoid that conversation face to face. Telehealth assessment moves[that process online](https://www.phoenix.ca/how-it-works) , though it still depends on completing lab work in person since blood cannot be drawn remotely.


Provincial coverage and availability of either path vary, so confirm current options with a healthcare provider in your province before choosing one.

## Final Thoughts On Testosterone, Peptides, And Treatment Paths


The body's testosterone, a prescribed dose, and an unsupervised steroid cycle all share a molecule, but the similarities stop there. Peptides and over the counter boosters do not carry the same evidence or oversight, so a lab test still provides more information than any product claim. If you are noticing changes in energy, mood, or muscle, your provider can help you figure out what is actually going on and where to go from there.


## FAQ


### Is testosterone a steroid or a hormone?


It's both. Testosterone is a steroid hormone: "steroid" describes its cholesterol-based chemical structure, while "hormone" describes its job as a chemical messenger in the body. The confusion usually comes from the slang use of "steroid" to mean anabolic steroid misuse, which is a different conversation involving doses far above what the body naturally produces.


### Is testosterone cypionate a steroid, and is it the same as TRT?


Yes, testosterone cypionate is a steroid in the chemical sense, the same cholesterol-based structure as any other form of testosterone, and it's also a controlled substance in Canada that requires a prescription. Whether it is part of TRT depends on context: use is TRT only when a licensed provider prescribes and monitors it after an assessment.


### Peptides vs steroids for muscle growth: are peptides considered steroids?


No. Peptides are short chains of amino acids, a different molecule family from steroid hormones like testosterone, and they aren't classified as steroids in bodybuilding or chemistry. That said, according to Drugs.com, no peptide is approved by the FDA to build muscle, and purity is a separate concern, as covered above.


### What supplements actually increase testosterone, and do testosterone boosters work?


Lifestyle factors like sleep, resistance training, a healthy body weight, and managing chronic stress tend to have better evidence for supporting testosterone levels than supplements do. Some[published reviews of testosterone boosters](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6920068/) suggest the evidence is limited and inconsistent that over-the-counter testosterone boosters raise levels in men whose testosterone is already in a normal range, so persistent symptoms are better checked with a blood test than a supplement bottle.


### Can you stop testosterone therapy once you start?


Yes, but it needs to happen under medical guidance, not on your own. Natural testosterone production can slow or stop during therapy since the body senses enough hormone circulating, so a licensed healthcare provider manages the stopping process to help natural production recover and to monitor symptoms along the way.
